market_question: Will Dan Cox win the 2026 Maryland Governor Republican primary election?
reasoning: Dan Cox lost the 2022 general election by a huge margin and is currently the only declared candidate for 2026, but the primary is over a year away and the Maryland GOP is likely to field more electable alternatives. His 2022 primary win was aided by Trump’s endorsement, which is not guaranteed in 2026, and his poor general-election performance weakens his frontrunner status. I judge his true probability below the market-implied 57.5%.
evidence_points: Cox lost the 2022 Maryland gubernatorial general election by nearly 30 points, making him a weak standard‑bearer.
No major opponent has yet announced, but the primary is in June 2026, leaving ample time for a credible challenger to emerge.
Trump’s 2022 endorsement was decisive; without it in 2026, Cox’s base may soften among primary voters.
sources_consulted: News reports of Dan Cox’s 2026 candidacy announcement (Baltimore Sun, early 2025)
General awareness of Maryland GOP dynamics (Hogan faction, recruitment of candidates)
